title: Match the sales motion to what a customer is worth
decision_task: Which acquisition motion a price point can afford.
applies_when: Choosing between self-serve, light-touch outreach and high-touch selling.
exclusions: When the play has its own measured CAC; use playMaths instead of the heuristic.
evidence_requirements: Hours per customer of the motion
missing_data_behavior: No measured CAC for the motion: use the CAC-aware price floor as a check, labelled heuristic.
Price unknown: motion fit is unknown.
alternatives_when_constrained: Missing economics: keep the static heuristic (scoring.ts:109; capacity.ts:14), labelled as a ClimbOS rule of thumb, not Skok's.

decision_branches.then: Self-serve and low-touch channels; human help only for top segments.

decision_branches.if: The play has its own measured CAC

implementation_steps: Compute the CAC-aware minimum price (DS-FX17) for the motion's expected CAC.
If price is below it, recommend lowering touch (demo video, comparison page, published objections, trial) or raising value or price.
Replace the static $25 and $300 thresholds with this computed check where inputs exist.
guardrails: Do not claim Skok's 10× per tier as a measured number for a given business; it was his rough estimate.
stop_conditions: Review when price or touch level changes.
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes

interpretation: Interpretation: ClimbOS already encodes Skok's direction but with fixed thresholds that are not derived from his work.
proposed_climbos_rule: Proposed rule: add a 'cac_price_floor' kind to decisions.ts calculate() using DS-FX17.
disagreements: Skok placed channel or partner sales in a danger zone. ClimbOS's partner plays (scoring.ts:119) are lighter-weight referrals; treat them as their own case.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
expected_behavior: P_min 73.49 > 49, so outreach does not pay back
Recommends self-serve or a lower-touch motion
hard_failure: Cites '10×' as a fact about this business

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
